description:
The house was built in 1515–1520 for the knight Hieronymus von Stauber, a financial expert in the service of the Fugger family, and granted the status of a noble seat, according to German Wikipedia, the main source for this chronology; it dates from the heyday of silver mining at Schwaz.

In 1694 it passed by marriage to Baron Ferdinand Fieger von Hirschberg, who enlarged it into a small palace around 1700. Its characteristic octagonal tower has a large Baroque onion dome, and rooms with stucco from around 1730 survive inside. Johann Gwercher bought it in 1802, which is why it is also called the "Gwercher Schlössl"; on 27 April 1873 it was bought by Josef Mayr, a carter and trader from Matrei am Brenner, whose descendants, the Mair family, still own it in the sixth generation.

Since 1938 it has been run as an inn and later as a castle hotel. Today it is a four-star family-run hotel with a Tyrolean restaurant and a beer garden by the Inn, a 10-minute walk from the old town of Schwaz.
history: Mitterhart was built in 1515–1520 for Hieronymus von Stauber, a financier of the Fugger family, at the time of the great silver mines of Schwaz. It passed by marriage to the Fieger family in 1694 and was enlarged into a small palace around 1700. Johann Gwercher bought it in 1802, giving it its other name, and in 1873 it was bought by Josef Mayr, whose family still owns it. Since 1938 it has been run as an inn and castle hotel.

faqs.question: Why is Schloss Mitterhart also called the Gwercher Schlössl?
faqs.answer: It takes that name from Johann Gwercher, who bought the house in 1802.

faqs.question: How old is Schloss Mitterhart?
faqs.answer: It was built in 1515–1520 for Hieronymus von Stauber, a financier of the Fugger family, and enlarged into a small palace around 1700.

meta_title: Mitterhart Castle, Vomp — Four-Star Manor Hotel on the Inn near Schwaz
meta_description: Stay at Mitterhart Castle, a 16th-century manor on the Inn opposite Schwaz, Tyrol — a four-star hotel with a Tyrolean restaurant. From approx. €186/night.

hotel.room_location_note: Rooms are in the manor house and its estate buildings; ask the hotel which building your room is in
hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** The hotel stands at Innhöfe 3, by the Inn river opposite Schwaz, in the municipality of Vomp in Tyrol; the old town of Schwaz is about a 10-minute walk away according to Booking, and the hotel is on the Inn Valley cycle path. Booking lists free private parking with electric charging.

**Rooms & rates:** From approx. €186/night for an 18 m² Double Room with a queen bed, a river view, a private bathroom and a flat-screen TV, with breakfast, one parking space and high-speed internet included on the non-refundable rate seen; a free-cancellation rate was around €207, and a 22 m² Deluxe Double Room around €197. Booking shows a small tax charge (about €5) separately.

**On-site:** A restaurant with Tyrolean cooking, a sun terrace and a beer garden by the river, free parking and free Wi-Fi.

**Good to know:** Rates were seen for one January 2027 night, a low-season date, so check your own dates on Booking. The house is a Renaissance manor rather than a fortified castle.

**Combine with:** [Tratzberg Castle](/castles/austria/tratzberg-castle), the Renaissance castle above Stans, about 6 km to the north-east, and [Schloss Ambras](/castles/austria/schloss-ambras) above Innsbruck, about 22 km to the south-west.
